text:
ashley: heads up — seeing large number of stalled gRPC streams between model pods in us-west-2 GPU cluster. requests start, emit a few tokens, then hang for ~30s before resuming. affects both pod->pod and node->node traffic. any ideas? @cheng
cheng: ugh. saw something like this last week on a node pair. what does `kubectl logs` show for the gRPC client side? any retransmits/dup acks in tcpdump?
ashley: digging, attaching small tcpdump excerpt:
```
IP 10.2.1.12.50010 > 10.2.2.34.60000: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12999, ack 6789, win 65535, length 654
IP (frag 1/2) 10.2.1.12 > 10.2.2.34: frag 1234:.....
IP 10.2.1.12.50010 > 10.2.2.34.60000: Flags [.], ack 6789, win 65535, length 0
kernel: TCP: possible SYN flooding...
```
cheng: that tcpdump shows fragmentation markers. are these nodes using an overlay (vxlan/geneve) or direct RDMA path?
maria: overlay + direct in some racks. last infra change: enabled jumbo frames on the RDMA NICs (MTU 9000) but overlays still default to 1500. if tunnel MTU < path MTU we can hit GSO/GRO fragmentation issues which break gRPC streaming behavior.
sre-lead: actionable checklist: 1) confirm link MTU on both endpoints (`ip link show dev <if>`), 2) check tunnel/encap MTU (`ip link`, `bridge link`), 3) run `iperf3 -M` or `ping -s` with DF to test PMTU, 4) capture pcap with `tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/xx.pcap host <peer>` to confirm fragments.
cheng: we had a similar outage — disabling GSO on the offending tunnel device temporarily unblocked streams. quick command we used: 
```bash
for d in vxlan0 eth0; do sudo ethtool -K $d gso off gro off tso off; done
```
that reduced fragmented skbs and streams resumed (CPU went up on nodes though).
ashley: tried the ethtool trick on a staging pair — streams recovered immediately, CPU spike ~8% but latency back to normal :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-319 created and assigned to ashley (priority P2)
sre-lead: long-term fix: enable proper PMTU discovery and/or MSS clamping on the tunnel egress so TCP/SYNs advertise smaller MSS. recommended kernel/sysctl and iptables bits: 
```bash
# enable probing so kernel will figure out proper path MTU
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1
# mangle table clamp MSS to PMTU for SYN packets leaving overlay
sudo iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```
also verify that CNIs are setting correct encap MTU when creating tunnels. if a host NIC is 9000 and tunnel is 1500 we must either clamp/adjust or set consistent MTU everywhere.
maria: logging/action items: - add node MTU drift alert to Console (retransmit rate > 5% && avg token latency > 500ms) - add a preflight check in the GPU node bootstrap that ensures overlay encap MTU >= host MTU or sets MSS clamp rules.
ashley: will roll a daemonset change to add TCPMSS clamp on all hosts in us-west-2 today and follow up with a CNI config patch to propagate encap MTU. will post PR and doc. thanks all.
